- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 2–4 days.
- If 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment (≥0.67) precede forecast, model tends to overcorrect; apply downward bias of 1–2% for next 5 days.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome for 5+ days, apply mean reversion: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is >75% of forecast, model is overconfident; adjust downward by 1–2% for next 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges direction; align forecast with sentiment trend shift, not absolute value.
